proofs.full_local_argument: For 1≤p<2 the fixed-norm conclusion is Proposition 3.2. For fixed p≥2 restrict epsilon≤min(epsilon_0,1/p); then p epsilon≤1 and Phi=p^(1/6)epsilon^(−1/3). Put a=p^(1/6)≥1 and x=k epsilon^(−1/3). The inequalities min(N,x)≤min(N,ax)≤a min(N,x) hold: the first is monotonicity, and the second follows by considering x≥N or x<N. Thus Theorem 3.1 yields tilde Theta_p(min(N,x)) after absorbing the fixed a and fixed-p logarithms. This does not hold uniformly along varying p. For the saturation variant simply substitute k=N−r, 1≤r<N, into Theorem 3.1. If (N−r)Phi≥N the finite-p minimum is N; for infinity it is N precisely when (N−r)/sqrt(epsilon)≥N. For fixed r and fixed admissible epsilon, k=N−r is Theta(N), so either minimum is Theta(N), with the theorem's logarithmic qualification. These are consequences relative to Proposition 3.2 and the linked uniform theorem, not independent proofs of their base lower or upper bounds.

assumptions: Exact measurable adaptive Av OR A^T u access; one product costs one, both cost two, b columns cost b; independent seed; free computation and storage.
Fix p before selecting constants or an accuracy threshold. No uniformity over 1≤p<2 or along varying p(epsilon) is asserted.
statement.conclusion: Proposition 3.2: c_p min(N,k epsilon^(−1/3))≤Q_p^*≤C_p min(N,k epsilon^(−1/3)) polylog(N,k,1/epsilon), for fixed 1≤p<2. Corollary 3.3: Q_p^*=tilde Theta_p(min(N,k epsilon^(−1/3))) for each fixed finite p. Corollary 3.4: writing Phi=epsilon^(−1/3)min(p^(1/6),epsilon^(−1/6)), Q_p^*(m,n,N−r,epsilon)=tilde Theta(min(N,(N−r)Phi)) for 2≤p<infinity; the spectral rate is tilde Theta(min(N,(N−r)/sqrt(epsilon))). Thus finite-p saturation occurs when (N−r)Phi≥N and spectral saturation when N−r≥N sqrt(epsilon). Fixed codimension and fixed admissible accuracy give linear complexity up to logarithms.
statement.objects_and_definitions: A in R^{m×n}, N=min(m,n), 1≤k<N. OPT_{p,k}(A)=min over rank-k orthogonal right P_* of ||A(I−P_*)||_{S_p}. Q_p^* is the least integer cap valid on every input and every seed, achieving ||A(I−P)||_{S_p}≤(1+epsilon)OPT_{p,k}(A) with probability ≥2/3 on every input, for arbitrary transcript-measurable rank-k orthogonal P in R^{n×n}.
statement.parameter_domains: Fixed finite 1≤p<infinity, 1≤k<N, 0<epsilon≤epsilon_p. For the p≥2 corollary derivation take epsilon≤min(epsilon_0,1/p). Saturation variant: k=N−r, integer 1≤r<N, 0<epsilon≤epsilon_0, 2≤p<infinity or p=infinity.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For each fixed 1≤p<2 there exist c_p,C_p,epsilon_p>0 such that the Proposition 3.2 inequalities hold for all dimensions, all 1≤k<N and 0<epsilon≤epsilon_p. Corollary 3.3 applies to every fixed finite p with p-dependent constants and sufficiently small epsilon. Corollary 3.4 instead uses the universal accuracy window and p≥2 regime of Theorem 3.1.
